Question: Which of the following analytical techniques can be used to distinguish an amorphous solid from a crystalline solid?

Options:
A. Heating the substances will show that an amorphous solid like glass softens gradually, while a crystalline solid melts at a specific temperature.
B. Microscopic examination reveals that a crystalline solid will deform plastically under tensile stress, while an amorphous solid will fracture in a brittle mode.
C. Spectroscopic analysis of UV-Vis absorbance can differentiate between amorphous and crystalline solids based on color changes.
D. X-ray diffraction can be used to distinguish a crystalline solid, which shows distinct diffraction patterns, while an amorphous solid only shows scattering.

A. Heating the substances will show that an amorphous solid like glass softens gradually, while a crystalline solid melts at a specific temperature.
   - This statement is true. Amorphous solids do not have a sharp melting point, whereas crystalline solids do.

B. Microscopic examination reveals that a crystalline solid will deform plastically under tensile stress, while an amorphous solid will fracture in a brittle mode.
   - This statement is not typically the method used to distinguish between amorphous and crystalline solids.

C. Spectroscopic analysis of UV-Vis absorbance can differentiate between amorphous and crystalline solids based on color changes.
   - UV-Vis absorbance is not commonly used to distinguish between amorphous and crystalline states.

D. X-ray diffraction can be used to distinguish a crystalline solid, which shows distinct diffraction patterns, while an amorphous solid only shows scattering.
   - This statement is true. X-ray diffraction is a standard technique to differentiate between crystalline and amorphous solids due to the presence of distinct patterns in crystalline solids.

Based on this analysis, options A and D are correct.
